page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.2xlarge is a compute-focused instance from the High Clock Speed family, designed for workloads requiring sustained CPU frequency. Built on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the server runs an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 3.1 GHz. Hardware resource allocation includes 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 16 GiB of RAM. This produces a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cache provisions consist of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB shared L3 cache, alongside vector support for AVX-512 extensions.

The hardware configuration bundles no local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. In synthetic testing, the instance produces average multi-core CPU performance, achieving 7,645.6 on stress-ng, 8,939.31 on PassMark CPU, and 4,795.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached read memory bandwidth measures 49.31 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reaches 6.88 GB/sec.

Workload evaluation highlights strengths in standard integer calculations, software build operations, and in-memory key-value caching, registering 7,143.0 on Geekbench Clang compilation and 7.45 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Tradeoffs appear under larger memory and tensor processing scenarios: prompt processing on a 7B parameter LLM degrades to 11.39 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators and restricted RAM capacity. The instance is suited for code compilation, CI/CD build environments, web serving, and application proxy layers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.2xlarge is a compute-focused virtual machine from the High Clock Speed family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture using KVM, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 16 GiB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio. The instance lacks integrated local storage and GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage and offering a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates balanced execution with a PassMark CPU score of 8,939.31 and Geekbench multi-core score of 4,795. Memory bandwidth reaches 49.31 GB/sec on uncached reads, supporting 7.45 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.88 GB/sec in static web serving. Given its compute density and AVX-512 instruction support, it is well suited for CPU-bound tasks such as code compilation, CI/CD runners, and application serving, though constrained for large-scale AI inference.
